drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A payments company has four hundred developers on Cursor, and they like it.
drills.answer_line: SAM: The answer is B. A change of owner is a reason for due diligence, not a verdict
drills.stem: Four hundred developers use Cursor and like it. The vendor-risk team notices Cursor changed owner in August and asks what to do. What do you advise?

options.A: Move everyone to Claude Code now, before the next audit
options.B: Keep Cursor for now, re-run due diligence on data routing, sub-processors and default models, and keep instructions in AGENTS.md so a later switch stays cheap
options.C: Do nothing: a change of owner does not change the product
options.D: Move everyone to Roo Code, because an open-source tool has no owner to change

drills.why: SpaceX closed its purchase of Cursor in August 2026. A new owner is a due-diligence trigger, not a verdict. A spends developer goodwill before there is an answer; C skips a fair risk question; D fails because Roo Code reportedly shut down and an open-source client still sends code to its model. If the review fails, AGENTS.md carries the instructions to the next tool.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.answer_line: SAM: Three out of four. Four is false.
drills.prompt: True or false? 1) Claude Code reads AGENTS.md when a repo has no CLAUDE.md. 2) MCP is still governed by Anthropic alone. 3) SKILL.md is supported by Codex, Copilot and Antigravity, though folder locations can differ. 4) Hooks written for Claude Code run unchanged in Codex.
drills.answer: 1) True. 2) False: it sits in the Agentic AI Foundation. 3) True. 4) False: similar event names, different config files, and Codex runs only command and MCP tool handlers.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A defence contractor's security team
drills.answer_line: SAM: That answers the question you prefer, not the one asked.
drills.stem: Security will approve a coding agent only if they can audit and build the client from source. Spend must draw down the AWS commitment; developers are content with OpenAI models. What fits?

options.C: Gemini CLI, which is also open source
options.D: Claude Code with a locked-down managed settings file

drills.why: The Codex CLI is Apache 2.0 and Codex is GA on Bedrock. Claude Code is not open source (A, D); managed settings constrain behaviour, not auditability. Gemini CLI now serves Google paid tiers, not an AWS bill.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A logistics company has six hundred developers
drills.answer_line: SAM: A and C. And notice the right answer is A W S's own tool.
drills.stem: Choose two. Six hundred developers on Amazon Q Developer Pro in their IDEs want newer Claude models than Q Developer offers. Which two pieces of advice are right?

options.A: Plan the move now: Q Developer IDE plugins reach end of support on 30 April 2027
options.B: Buy more Q Developer seats for a team joining next quarter
options.C: Evaluate Kiro, the AWS successor, which carries the newer Claude models
options.D: Stay on Q Developer and wait for the newer Claude models to arrive there
options.E: Move the developers to personal Gemini CLI accounts

drills.why: Q Developer is retiring, and Claude models from Opus 4.7 onward are Kiro-only. New sign-ups closed in May 2026 (B); D waits for models that will not come; the personal Gemini CLI tier was cut off (E).

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A C I O cites the Menlo figure
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. A leans on a number that cannot choose between the two products.
drills.stem: A CIO cites Menlo's figure, Claude Code and Codex at about 70% of coding spend, and wants to standardise on Claude Code on that basis alone. Best response?

options.B: Note the figure does not split Claude Code from Codex, Menlo is an Anthropic investor, and a pilot on their own repos is the better basis
options.C: Dismiss the report as investor marketing
options.D: Use OpenRouter token rankings instead, since they are measured, not surveyed

drills.why: The combined figure cannot pick between the two products and comes from an Anthropic investor's survey of about 400 US enterprises. C discards real evidence; OpenRouter skews to cost-sensitive developers, not enterprise spend.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments, and the customer question each one hands you.
drills.answer_line: ALEX: The convergence, Codex, the platform vendors' agents
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and the customer question each one hands you.
drills.answer: Convergence: where do your instructions live? Codex: sandbox on by default, or the source? Platform vendors: which vendor do you already pay, and is your tool retiring? Independents and data: what does this number measure?
